Yongbyon Nuclear Complex.name: Yongbyon Nuclear Complex
Yongbyon Nuclear Complex.note: As of April 2026: Enrichment building expansion complete, new centrifuge hall operational. 5 MWe reactor and IRT-2000 both running. Thermal signatures consistent with increased plutonium/HEU production.

Sinpo South Shipyard.name: Sinpo South Shipyard
Sinpo South Shipyard.note: As of May 2025: Hero Kim Kun Ok SLBM submarine exited drydock after 2+ years of fitting-out but was still not operational. New submarine construction begun in separate bay. NK Pro satellite analysis (Oct 20 2026) separately reports North Korea's Nampho Shipyard missed a deadline earlier in Oct 2026 to launch a 5,000-ton naval destroyer, with hull sections visible at two potential outdoor assembly areas. 38 North analysis published Oct 30 documents public display of a vessel described as a 'Tactical Nuclear Attack' submarine. Kim Jong Un inspected Nampho Shipyard on Nov 7 (reported Nov 8 by KCNA), announcing a new warship under construction larger than the destroyer built last year. NK News reported on Nov 6 that North Korea has expanded warship construction to a third shipyard. 38 North published analysis on Nov 11 of the Choe Hyon destroyer and its strategic implications for the West Sea Fleet. NK News identified a second major east-coast naval base project on Nov 13, beyond the Munchon-area site Kim inspected on Nov 12.

THAAD Site — Seongju County.name: THAAD Site — Seongju County
THAAD Site — Seongju County.note: As of March 2026: All 6 THAAD launchers were redeployed to the Middle East amid Iran tensions. At least 2 launchers may have returned to Seongju by late March 2026. Battery operational status remains uncertain. This report is over six months old and may not reflect the current state.

Sohae Satellite Launch Station.name: Sohae Satellite Launch Station
Sohae Satellite Launch Station.note: As of March 2026: 2,500 kN engine test stand firing observed. Two villages razed for facility expansion. New seaport and large assembly building nearing completion. This report is over six months old and may not reflect the current state.

Punggye-ri Nuclear Test Site.name: Punggye-ri Nuclear Test Site
Punggye-ri Nuclear Test Site.note: As of November 2025: ROK Defense Intelligence Agency assessed Tunnel No. 3 is test-ready and a nuclear test can be conducted at any time upon political decision. Site maintained at high readiness since mid-2024. This report is over six months old and may not reflect the current state.

Tumangang–Khasan (NK-Russia border).name: Tumangang–Khasan (NK-Russia border)
Tumangang–Khasan (NK-Russia border).note: As of March 2026: Road bridge construction accelerated, completion target moved to Summer 2026. Passenger rail service resumed mid-2025. Ore and tank car traffic at highest levels since project began. This report is over six months old and may not reflect the current state. Russian Transport Ministry applications filed Nov 13 for a 14-daily-round-trip Vladivostok-Rason bus route over the new vehicle bridge, with experts noting the service will likely transport DPRK workers more than Russian tourists.

Sinuiju–Dandong (NK-China border).name: Sinuiju–Dandong (NK-China border)
Sinuiju–Dandong (NK-China border).note: 38 North satellite imagery from October 16 confirms trucks traversing the New Yalu River (DPRK-Friendship) Bridge one day after the October 15 official opening, marking the start of commercial vehicle traffic. Daily NK reports (Oct 31) that North Korean trucks have still not joined Chinese cargo trucks on the bridge two weeks after the Oct 15 opening; North Korean transport officials are still preparing vehicles. North Korea-China trade reached $299M in September 2026, the second-highest monthly total in 2026. Kim Jong Un crossed the New Yalu River Bridge on October 24 during his unannounced visit to Dandong. Daily NK reports on Nov 3, 2026 that North Korea is courting Chinese investors to build hotels and shopping complexes in Sinuiju. NK News reports a surge in North Korean delegations visiting China, putting commercial ties in focus. Daily NK reports Nov 12 that Chinese truck drivers who relied on side income ferrying parcels across the new bridge are souring on operations due to tighter customs checks and movement controls since the October opening. Huanghai Automobile's Dandong bus factory announced it is operating at full capacity on Nov 13 following Kim Jong Un's October visit, raising questions about potential vehicle exports to the DPRK.

Rason SEZ.name: Rason SEZ
Rason SEZ.note: As of November 2025: Chinese businesspeople re-entry to Rason SEZ expanded. Coal exports through Rason at highest levels in years throughout 2025. Arms export berth also active. This report is over six months old and may not reflect the current state.

Yellow Sea NLL.name: Yellow Sea NLL
Yellow Sea NLL.note: As of September 26, 2025: 140m DPRK merchant vessel Toksong crossed the Northern Limit Line near Baengnyeong Island, advanced 5km south. ROK Navy fired approximately 60 warning shots; vessel retreated after 1 hour. ROK Marine Corps Commandant Gen. Ju Il-suk stated October 20 2026 that North Korea has made 'various changes' to forces facing South Korea's border islands, with Seoul stepping up surveillance along the maritime border. 38 North satellite imagery published October 29 shows North Korea continuing to install new fencing along its border. North Korean propaganda loudspeakers were visible at two border locations on Nov 4 from Odusan Unification Observatory and Key Observatory in Gyeonggi Province. ROK Joint Chiefs confirmed Nov 6 that a drifting North Korean fishing vessel was spotted in international waters off Ulleung Island on Nov 3 and is under investigation.

Yellow Sea PMZ.name: Yellow Sea PMZ
Yellow Sea PMZ.note: As of January 27-28, 2026: Atlantic Amsterdam (converted oil rig, Chinese aquaculture platform) relocated out of the Provisional Measures Zone to Weihai shipyard following President Lee Jae-myung's Beijing state visit. Two giant aquaculture cages (Shen Lan 1, Shen Lan 2) and 13 buoys remain in the PMZ. This report is over six months old and may not reflect the current state.

Vostochny/Dunai (Russian Far East).name: Vostochny/Dunai (Russian Far East)
Vostochny/Dunai (Russian Far East).note: As of January 2026: Arms shipments slowed due to ice — one Russian vessel (likely Angara or Lady R) visited Rason, docked January 14 at arms export berth. Cargo routed to Vostochny. Since September 2023: 64 voyages by 4 vessels (Angara, Maria, Maya-1, Lady R) delivered approximately 15,800 containers (approximately 4.2-5.8 million munitions) from Rajin to Vostochny/Dunai. This report is over six months old and may not reflect the current state. Russian Transport Ministry applications filed Nov 13 for a Vladivostok-Rason bus route operating 14 daily round trips.
